top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct, well-defined idea (Katori's proposal and realisation, Ye's development to the 10^-18 level) that has been reproduced and surpassed independently in several laboratories, with theory and experiment in close agreement and every systematic understood. A two-name allocation with a citation scoped to invention and realisation avoids overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is a genuine, mature achievement but carries a narrower consensus, an unresolved priority question (Hasan, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and a closer 2016 precedent, so it ranks second; an award in a year with a clean, widely supported candidate is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am WACQT director and work in superconducting circuits, but have no tie to the lattice-clock candidates or to the topological-insulator candidates
